extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the journal Graphs and Combinatorics (Springer Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting a research manuscript (mathematics) to the Springer journal Graphs and Combinatorics, covering formatting, metadata, declarations, and post-acceptance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript originality and exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies: that the work described has not been published before; that it is not under consideration for publication anywhere else; that its publication has been approved by all co-authors, if any, as well as by the responsible authorities – tacitly or explicitly – at the institute where the work has been carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions failing these conditions may be rejected; the publisher will not be held legally responsible for related claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages that have already been published elsewhere are required to obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both the print and online format and to include evidence that such permission has been granted when submitting their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material received without such evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Please follow the hyperlink 'Submit manuscript' and upload all of your manuscript files following the instructions given on the screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all files requested by the submission system are uploaded; follow on-screen instructions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete editable source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure you provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision. Failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in your article not being considered for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For manuscript text always submit in common word processing formats such as .docx or LaTeX; include all style files and figures; uploaded source files are transferred to publisher upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents — title
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be concise and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place title on title page along with other required metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents — author information and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: The name(s) of the author(s); The affiliation(s) of the author(s), i.e. institution, (department), city, (state), country; A clear indication and an active e-mail address of the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If address information is provided with the affiliation(s) it will also be published. For (temporarily) unaffiliated authors only city and country are captured, not e-mail unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID
rubrics_metrics.description: If available, the 16-digit ORCID of the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ORCID(s) on the title page; they will be published with the article if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on Large Language Models (LLMs) and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria. Notably an attribution of authorship carries with it accountability for the work, which cannot be effectively applied to LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (or suitable alternative) of the manuscript. AI-assisted copy editing does not need declaration; there must always be human accountability for the final text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words. The abstract should not contain any undefined abbreviations or unspecified references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some life-science articles, trial registration number and date must be included (or stated as retrospectively registered) — included only when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide 4 to 6 keywords which can be used for indexing purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose keywords that reflect content for indexing and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: The following statements must be included in your submitted manuscript under the heading 'Statements and Declarations' for inclusion in the published paper. Submissions that do not include relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required declarations include Funding, Competing interests, Ethics approval, Consent, Data/Material/Code availability, and Authors’ contribution statements where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to disclose financial or non-financial interests that are directly or indirectly related to the work submitted for publication. Interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work should be reported; interests outside 3 years must be disclosed if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the submitted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed examples (funding, employment, stocks, consultancy, patents, advisory roles, board positions, etc.). Editorial Board Members must declare competing interests and may be excluded from handling peer review; submissions from editors are handled by other editors and subject to same review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe any sources of funding that have supported the work. The statement should include details of any grants received (please give the name of the funding agency and grant number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording templates provided; when no funding, examples of statements indicating no funding are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a statement that specifies the contribution of every author to the research and preparation of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: who did conception, material preparation, data collection/analysis, drafting, and approval of final manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text formatting and language
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be written in English and submitted in LaTeX. Please use Springer’s LaTeX macro package and choose the formatting option 'smallextended'. The submission should include the original source (including all style files and figures) and a PDF version of the compiled output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uploaded source files will be automatically compiled into a single PDF for review; the compiled PDF will be used for peer-review purposes but source files are required for production upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent hierarchical numbering (e.g., 1., 1.1, 1.1.1) is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undefined abbreviations in abstract and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can be used to give additional information, which may include the citation of a reference included in the reference list. They should not consist solely of a reference citation, and they should never include the bibliographic details of a reference. They should also not contain any figures or tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to the text are numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values). Footnotes to the title or the authors are not given reference symbols. Always use footnotes instead of endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. should be placed in a separate section before the reference list. The names of funding organizations should be written in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a separate 'Acknowledgments' section; provide full funder names and grant numbers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX submission specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: All source files you upload in the online submission system will be automatically compiled into a single PDF file to be approved by you at the end of the submission process. Do not use subfolders for your LaTeX submission, e.g. for figures or bibliographic files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further tips available at Springer LaTeX Support hub and submission system help pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets. Examples given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numbered citations like [3], [1-3, 7], etc., placed where appropriate in prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list contents and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of references should only include works that are cited in the text and that have been published or accepted for publication. Personal communications and unpublished works should only be mentioned in the text. The entries in the list should be numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links (e.g. 'https://doi.org/abc'). Use standard journal name abbreviations per ISSN LTWA; if unsure, use full journal title. Examples for journal article, article by DOI, book, book chapter, and online document provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are to be numbered using Arabic numerals. Tables should always be cited in text in consecutive numerical order. For each table, please supply a table caption (title) explaining the components of the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any previously published material by giving the original source in the form of a reference at the end of the table caption. Footnotes to tables should be indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values) and included beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification codes (MSC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriate number of MSC codes should be provided. The Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) is used to categorize items covered by the two reviewing databases, Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt MATH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MSC codes after the Abstract section; refer to www.ams.org/msc for codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific style for mathematical notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the standard mathematical notation for formulae, symbols etc.: Italic for single letters that denote mathematical constants, variables, and unknown quantities; Roman/upright for numerals, operators, and punctuation, and commonly defined functions or abbreviations, e.g., cos, det, e or exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d (for derivative); Bold for vectors, tensors, and matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conventional typographic distinctions to ensure clarity of symbols and operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests — details and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Interests that should be considered and disclosed include funding, employment, financial interests (stocks, consultation fees, patents), and non-financial interests (editorial positions, advisory boards, consulting for educational purposes, expert witness, mentoring relations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guideline: any undeclared financial interest that could embarrass the author if publicly known should be disclosed. Examples of wording for various cases are provided; primary research articles require a disclosure statement; review articles require a disclosure statement; other article types may require one depending on content.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-acceptance procedures and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, your article will be exported to Production to undergo typesetting. You will receive two e-mails: one to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights and payment; a second with a link to proofs once typesetting is completed. The article publishing agreement will require either granting an exclusive licence or transferring copyright, depending on journal ownership/policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offprints can be ordered. Online color illustrations are free; color in print may incur extra costs. The proof stage is to check for typesetting/conversion errors — substantial changes in content are not allowed without Editor approval; further changes post-publication only via Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice and open access publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows you to publish open access in Springer Nature journals. Open Choice articles do not require transfer of copyright as the copyright remains with the author. In opting for open access, the author(s) agree to publish the article under a Creative Commons license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APCs vary by journal; Open Choice increases visibility and may aid compliance with funder mandates. See journal-specific Open Access pages for fees, funding and license details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of declarations placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The above should be summarized in a statement and placed in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list under a heading of 'Funding' and/or 'Competing interests'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all authors have the same (or no) conflicts and/or funding it is sufficient to use one blanket statement. Examples of wording for funding, no funding, interests to declare, and nothing to declare are provided.
